text:
tara (PM): Quick brainstorm: for the next release we need a predictable surge protection model that doesn't tank demos or create billing surprises. Can we outline options?

leo (RevOps): TL;DR: customers want safety (hard caps) + flexibility (one-off top-ups). Ops wants automated enforcement. We should price by 'credits' consumed per token-equivalent.

e than (Eng): Enforcement modes: 
- soft-throttle: reduce concurrency / insert 100-500ms delay (slow-lane)
- hard-cap: immediate 429 when credits exhausted
- fallback-model: route to smaller model variant when available
Each has different cost/latency tradeoffs.

tara (PM): My recommended default: soft-throttle for 1 minute, then hard-cap. For enterprise deals, allow fallback-model + auto-topup if contract permits.

greta (Sales): Field note: SVB-ish customers prefer spend caps over rate caps. They want a monthly invoice ceiling and a separate emergency top-up flow. Also ask for a self-serve top-up in the console + support-assisted option.

nina (Legal): Any top-up must be auditable and flagged as "non-refundable" unless explicitly agreed. We need explicit opt-in in contract for auto-topups. Add abuse detection guardrails.

meter-bot: billing-bot: New meter hook available: promo-code credits and manual top-up events are now emitted to `billing.events` topic.

ethan (Eng): Sketch of API headers we'll return so clients can react client-side: 
```
X-Credits-Remaining: 125000
X-Soft-Throttle: true
X-Fallback-Model: rdm-small or empty
X-Estimated-Spend-This-Month: 42.73
Retry-After: 30
```
Clients can surface a warning banner when Credits-Remaining < 5% of cap.

leo (RevOps): Pricing thought: three SKU shapes: Hobby (monthly cap $25), Scale (cap $1,200), Enterprise (cap negotiable). Credits price with stepped volume discounts. Also plan an "emergency top-up" SKU ($X per 10k credits) with immediate availability.

greta (Sales): For pilots we prefer a temporary promo code that gives 50k credits and avoids contract work. If we need contract exceptions, keep them limited to named accounts only.

tara (PM): Launch checklist (minimal):
- UI: console cap + top-up flow + promo-code UX
- API: headers + error semantics documented
- Billing: immediate consumption + audit logs + non-refundable flag
- Legal: clause templates for auto-topup & refunds
- Ops: alerts for spend>80% and sudden spike detection runbook
- Sales: demo mode promo codes for pilots

nina (Legal): I'll draft two short clauses: (1) Monthly cap and overage behavior; (2) Emergency top-ups (non-refundable, immediate). Will share by EOD.

ethan (Eng): Dev tasks: meter hook for credits, soft-throttle implementation (configurable delay window), header plumbing, and fallback routing. ETA for a prototype: Wednesday EOD.

leo (RevOps): Dashboard KPIs at launch: credit_burn_rate, caps_hit_count, soft_throttle_events, emergency_topup_count, refunds_requested. Add alert when caps_hit_count rises too fast.

greta (Sales): I'll nominate two pilot customers and gather acceptable demo behavior (no 429s during live demo).

tara (PM): Decisions so far: default enforcement = soft-throttle -> hard-cap; provide console top-ups + promo code path for pilots; require explicit contract opt-in for auto-topup. Next sync Thursday 10am PT.

meter-bot: deploy-bot: Metering feature flag will be rolled out to canary orgs Tuesday 03:00 UTC.

tara (PM): All right, please add any missing risks here. Biggest open: exact credit pricing and how we communicate spend estimates to customers. We'll finalize pricing in pricing guild later this week. Thanks all :rocket:
